name: Game-help aid (B1-B9)
hypothesis: Pointing the player at the in-game help and keybinding list shortens keybinding and menu hunts.

uptake_metric.name: memory.records
uptake_metric.definition: Procedure records written to the memory store, which is where the player kept keybinding procedures

notes: Lost runs are excluded. The aid's own action, reading the in-game help, is out of play, so the target metric is confounded by the change itself. The mode reader has since passed re-validation, so the stall counts are no longer provisional. Next: measure hunts by screen identity, not by mode.

name: Zoom aid (A1-A6)
hypothesis: A zoomed re-read of a frame cuts perception errors (misread needs, creatures and text).

uptake_metric.name: tools.calls
uptake_metric.definition: player_source calls that passed a zoom argument

notes: The aid was never used, so it cannot be judged. Next: find out why the player did not use it before trying again.

name: Provider retry fixes (#378-#380)
hypothesis: Retrying a message-less 429, a balance-citing 429 and a stream that fails before its first event stops runs ending on provider errors.

uptake_metric.name: host.retry_share
uptake_metric.definition: Share of requests that were retries, aborts or non-tool stops

notes: Five runs (A2 and four game-help runs) ended on provider errors before the fixes landed. After them no run ended on a provider error; one reflection run was lost to a custody stop, which is not a provider error. Retries fired as designed in aidC1. The runs ran in order, so the comparison mixes the fixes with run order and provider drift.

name: Reflection lineage (C1-C6)
hypothesis: Carrying reflection advice into each admission stops a survivor repeating the same failure.
notes: Advice records were carried into each admission, but whether the player followed them cannot be measured without the player stating its intent, which is deferred until after #382.
